title: Magneto-Caloric effect and Multiple magnetic phases in Al doped Ni2MnSn0.75Al0.25 Heusler Alloys
authors: Satya Vijay Kumar, Simran, Madhusmita Jena, Mehroosh Fatema, Atul Gangwar, Srishti Dixit, Umashankar Rajput, Nisha Shahi, Chetna Gautam, Sanjay Singh, Anup K. Ghosh, Sandip Chatterjee
abstract: Among Heusler compounds,Ni based alloys have been extensively investigated because they exhibit desirable properties such as high Curie temperatures, which are advantageous for advanced magnetic and spintronic devices.The effect of Al substitution on the magnetic ground state of Ni2MnSn was investigated using the Ni2MnSn0.75Al0.25 Heusler alloy.Temperature-dependent magnetisation measurements identify a second-order paramagnetic to ferromagnetic transition at TC is 734K,followed by a first-order martensitic transformation near 263K,demonstrating strong magnetostructural coupling.Curie Weiss analysis yields a positive Weiss temperature theta CW is 746.4K and an effective magnetic moment of 6.82muB,confirming the predominance of ferromagnetic exchange interactions. The bifurcation between the ZFC and FCW magnetization curves,together with non saturating hysteretic M vs H loops, indicates the coexistence of competing ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic interactions.Further magnetic investigations establish the formation of an interacting reentrant cluster glass state accompanied by an exchange-bias effect.The observed magnetic behavior is attributed to the modification of Mn Mn exchange interactions induced by Al substitution and the associated atomic disorder,resulting in a complex magnetic ground state.
summary: This work characterizes the Al-doped Ni2MnSn Heusler alloy, revealing strong coupling between its crystal structure and magnetic properties. Key findings include multiple phase transitions (paramagnetic-to-ferromagnetic and martensitic) and evidence of a complex reentrant cluster-glass state due to competing magnetic interactions. The research demonstrates potential for magnetocaloric applications based on these coupled transitions.
main_problem: The study investigates the complex magnetic ground state, magnetocaloric effect, and multiple magnetic phases in Al-doped Ni2MnSn Heusler alloys.
main_result: The alloy exhibits strong magnetostructural coupling, evidence of competing ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic interactions leading to a reentrant cluster-glass state, and measurable magnetocaloric response near phase transitions.
method: Measurements include temperature-dependent magnetization (ZFC/FC), Differential Scanning Calorimetry (DSC), X-ray Photoemission Spectroscopy (XPS), and calculation of magnetic entropy change ($\Delta S_M$).
model_or_system: The physical system is the intermetallic Heusler alloy Ni2MnSn0.75Al0.25, which undergoes structural changes (martensitic transformation) coupled with complex magnetic ordering.
key_observables: Curie temperature ($T_C \approx 734	ext{ K}$), martensitic transition temperature ($\sim 263	ext{ K}$), magnetocaloric entropy change ($\Delta S_M$), and evidence of exchange bias.
important_parameters: Weiss temperature ($	heta_{	ext{CW}}=746.4	ext{ K}$), effective magnetic moment ($6.82\ \mu_B$), and field exponents ($n=0.784$ to $1.07$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the observed phenomena are governed by competing FM/AFM interactions modified by Al substitution and atomic disorder.
figures_summary: Figures show XRD patterns confirming crystal structure, SEM/EDX images verifying composition, and magnetization curves illustrating magnetic transitions and hysteresis loops.
paper_structure: The paper systematically characterizes the material using structural (XRD, SEM), electronic (XPS), and thermodynamic/magnetic measurements (Magnetization, DSC, $\Delta S_M$ calculation) to map out multiple coupled phase transitions.
why_interesting: The study of reentrant cluster-glass states and magnetostructural coupling in Heusler alloys provides a rich experimental platform for understanding how structural disorder influences complex magnetic ground states, relevant to frustrated magnetism models.
